---
title: "Gateway"
sidebarTitle: "Overview"
description: "The software factory: custom apps, agents, and automations assembled from SDK primitives on top of the World Model"
---

**Gateway** is Oxygen's software factory, the top layer of Oxygen Nexus.
[Pylon](/guide/build/data-infrastructure) lands and shapes the data, and
[Matrix](/guide/build/world-model), the World Model, defines what it means.
Gateway is where the operating software a business runs on is built over
that model: [custom apps](/guide/build/custom-apps),
[agents](/guide/build/agents), and [automations](/guide/build/automations).

Every product built in Gateway is assembled from the same small set of SDK
primitives, over the same World Model, on the same hosted runtime. A new app
for a new customer is a new composition of those primitives rather than a new
stack: no backend to stand up, no authentication to implement, and no metric
definitions to rewrite.

| Layer | Name | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 03 | **Gateway** · Software Factory | Build the software: apps, agents, automations |
| 02 | **Matrix** · World Model | Model the business: physics, calibration, control |
| 01 | **Pylon** · Data Infrastructure | Land and shape the data: Airway, Airhouse, Airform, Airconductor |

## The primitives

An app is a React + Vite bundle built with the [Oxygen SDK](/guide/build/sdk)
(`@oxy-hq/sdk`), plus any server-side functions it ships with. The SDK
exposes a fixed set of primitives:

| Primitive | What it does | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Data hooks** | `useQuery` runs SQL; `useSemanticQuery` queries measures and dimensions from the semantic model. | [Hooks](/guide/build/sdk/hooks#reading-data) |
| **World Model interface** | `useWorldModel` navigates a metric into its components and drivers, explains a move, sizes an opportunity, and drills into a segment. `useBaseline`, `usePredict`, and `useProjection` run scenario forecasts over the metric tree. | [World Model interface](/guide/build/sdk/world-model), [Scenario forecasting](/guide/build/sdk/hooks#scenario-forecasting) |
| **Agent hooks and components** | `useAgentRun` runs an agent; `<OxyChat>` and `<OxyAnswer>` embed chat and answers. | [Hooks](/guide/build/sdk/hooks#running-agents) |
| **Automation runs** | `useProcedureRun` runs a multi-step automation. | [Hooks](/guide/build/sdk/hooks#running-agents) |
| **Oxygen Functions** | Server-side TypeScript on a managed V8 runtime, invoked by a user, a schedule, an Airway step, or a verified webhook. Writes facts to Airhouse (`ctx.airhouse`), records to the org's Postgres (`ctx.oltp`), and files to app storage (`ctx.storage`). | [Functions](/guide/build/sdk/functions) |
| **Identity and publish** | `oxy-app.json` names the app; `oxyc publish` versions and deploys the interface and its functions together. | [SDK](/guide/build/sdk#deploy) |

## Why primitives scale

Building operating software per customer usually means rebuilding the same
infrastructure each time: a backend, authentication, a data pipeline, metric
definitions, and hosting. Gateway moves each of those into the platform, so
the per-customer work is the part that is actually specific to the customer.

- **The model is shared.** An app does not define its metrics. It reads
  them from the World Model, so every app, agent, and dashboard uses the same
  definitions, and a second app for another team or customer starts with
  them already in place.
- **Cross-cutting concerns are platform features.** Access rides on the
  viewer's Oxygen session and is scoped to project membership, so a bundle
  carries no API key. Webhooks are verified before a function runs, every
  route invocation is rate-limited and audited, and publishing is one
  versioned step.
- **The surface is constrained.** An app reaches data only through the SDK
  hooks and the function context. Each function declares its
  [capabilities](/guide/build/sdk/functions#capabilities) in `oxy-app.json`,
  every capability fails closed, and `oxyc publish` refuses a function that
  calls one it did not declare. A bounded surface is what makes apps written
  quickly, including by coding agents, reviewable and safe to ship.
- **Data written by apps feeds the model.** Facts an app records land in
  Airhouse in the app's own schema, where they can be modeled as measures.
  The work done in an app becomes part of what the World Model can explain
  and control.

The result is that the marginal cost of an app falls with each one built.
The infrastructure under the second app is the same as under the first, and
only the composition and the customer-specific logic change.
